criteria.quote: Jigglypuff tunes its voice to your brain waves.
criteria.revision: Replace it with: "Jigglypuff can freely change its voice’s wavelength—and its sound waves match the brain waves of deep sleep." This preserves the unusual reveal without claiming it specifically tunes to the viewer.

criteria.quote: Its vocal cords can freely change the wavelength of its voice.
criteria.revision: Make the fact more uniquely Jigglypuff by combining the two concrete details: "Jigglypuff’s vocal cords freely adjust its voice’s wavelength to make foes most drowsy."

criteria.quote: Why tune its voice to sleeping brains instead of just singing?
criteria.revision: Replace the unsupported motive-based loop with: "What happens when an opponent does not easily fall asleep?" This is answered by the research’s claim that Jigglypuff keeps singing and may endanger its life.

criteria.quote: It adjusts until the wavelength makes foes most drowsy.
criteria.revision: Reorder the scenes so the danger follows the sleep mechanism, then use the precise evidence: "If an opponent does not easily fall asleep, Jigglypuff cannot breathe—and its life is endangered." This raises the stakes instead of repeating wavelength facts.

criteria.quote: The trick is matching sound waves with deep-sleep brain waves.
criteria.revision: Reveal this after the wavelength setup, then add the less expected contrast: "Its vocal range exceeds 12 octaves, but each Jigglypuff’s singing skill depends on its own effort." This changes the image from an automatic sleep machine to a Pokémon with individual vocal skill.

criteria.quote: Its voice can shift; The patterns match; It finds the sleep setting.
criteria.revision: Cut one of the repeated wavelength scenes and replace it with a distinct fact: "Jigglypuff never pauses to breathe while singing." Follow that with the life-endangerment detail so each scene adds new information.

criteria.quote: Jigglypuff's song matches deep-sleep brain waves, but resisting it can put Jigglypuff's life at risk.
criteria.revision: End with a factual tradeoff rather than restating the match: "Its voice can make foes most drowsy—but if they do not fall asleep, Jigglypuff may keep singing until it cannot breathe." This resolves the sleep mechanism with its specific cost.

criteria.quote: Smart sleep mechanic or dangerous song?
criteria.revision: Replace it with a grounded choice: "Would you buy a Jigglypuff lullaby recording—or avoid it because its song makes listeners sleepy?" The research explicitly says recordings are sold and that the song induces sleep, creating two credible reactions.
